methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective comparative cohort of 86 patients (29 melanomas, 57 nevi) from a single national ocular oncology center with clearly specified inclusion criteria (>=5 years follow-up for nevi, ICD-10-based diagnoses), adequate exclusion criteria for image quality, and clear separation between the cohort and MelAInoma training data. Statistical approach is appropriate: linear regression, Jonckheere-Terpstra one-sided trend test, univariable and multivariable logistic regression, Tjur's R2, AIC, Hosmer-Lemeshow calibration, DeLong test for AUC comparison in sensitivity analyses, and bootstrap internal validation (2000 resamples) with optimism-corrected calibration slope. Limitations include single-center design, no histopathologic confirmation of diagnoses, relatively small cohort with imbalanced MOLES categories, and potential shared-feature incorporation between MOLES and reference diagnosis (authors acknowledge this).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort validation of two diagnostic/triage tools in a referral center, corresponding to Oxford LoE 2b (individual cohort including validation study). Clinical relevance is direct: both MOLES and MelAInoma are intended for non-expert triage of pigmented choroidal lesions, and the findings inform referral-triage practice, especially in settings lacking multimodal imaging. The authors explicitly acknowledge the need for multicenter prospective validation before broader adoption.

reporting_quality.justification: As a diagnostic accuracy study, STARD is the applicable standard. The manuscript clearly reports index tests (MOLES, MelAInoma), reference standard (expert multimodal diagnosis), participant flow, inclusion/exclusion, imaging modality subgroup analyses, calibration, discrimination (AUC with 95% CI), and limitations including reference-standard circularity. Formal STARD checklist adherence is not declared. Ethical approval is provided. No data-sharing statement or code repository is mentioned for the MelAInoma algorithm (which is proprietary software, v0.1 Eyedentity AB), limiting reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: Both MOLES (Damato et al., refs 20-24) and MelAInoma (authors' prior work, refs 15, 19) have been previously published and evaluated. The novelty here is the head-to-head comparison of the two triage systems in the same cohort under expert-applied conditions, with bootstrap internal validation and imaging-modality subgroup analyses. This is a meaningful incremental contribution that establishes complementarity between the two tools, but not a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is very well written, precisely worded, and appropriately hedged. Structure is clear, tables and figures are referenced systematically, and limitations are extensive and self-critical. The authors carefully distinguish statistical significance from clinical utility and discuss threshold-dependent trade-offs. Publication-ready with only minor polish needed.

key_strengths: Well-defined external cohort (86 patients) independent of MelAInoma training data with >=5-year nevus follow-up requirement
Appropriate statistical framework with bootstrap internal validation, optimism correction, and calibration assessment
Head-to-head comparison under expert-applied MOLES conditions acknowledges the performance ceiling of manual scoring
Transparent discussion of shared-feature incorporation between MOLES and the reference standard
Imaging-modality subgroup sensitivity analyses with DeLong test
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design limits generalizability; no multicenter prospective validation
No histopathologic confirmation of diagnoses; reference standard is expert multimodal clinical diagnosis
Relatively small sample (n=86) with imbalanced MOLES categories may inflate CIs for category-specific estimates
MelAInoma is proprietary software (v0.1); no data or model parameters shared for independent replication
Cohort skews toward referral population of a national center; generalization to primary care uncertain
chief_reviewer.rationale: Rigorous comparative diagnostic study with transparent statistics and hedged clinical interpretation; appropriate for a tier-2 ophthalmology/oncology journal after minor revisions clarifying STARD adherence and data/model availability.
